title: How much of each ingredient do fifteen guests need?
description: A dish made for a family of five is scaled up for fifteen guests. The video finds one factor of change and multiplies every ingredient by it, then checks that rice and dal stay in the same ratio.
teaching_notes: One idea: one factor of change, guests divided by family size, multiplies every ingredient. Watch for students who scale only one ingredient or who add the extra guests to each amount.

video_script.why: The child can find a missing term, and now scales a whole recipe with one factor of change.
video_script.substitution: Divide the number of guests by the family size, then multiply every ingredient by that factor.
video_script.anchor: a family dish for five people, with rice and dal, from the book's activity
video_script.payoff_line: Multiply every ingredient by the same factor, guests divided by family size

final_answer.value: Multiply every ingredient by the same factor, guests ÷ family size
final_answer.spoken: multiply every ingredient by the same factor, guests divided by family size

never_show: adding 10 to every ingredient, marked as right
maths_rules: sample family of 5: 2 cups rice, 1 cup dal
check: rice to dal is 2 : 1 before and 6 : 3 = 2 : 1 after
each child's own dish and family size give different numbers; the method is the same
video_script.design: One idea: one factor for every ingredient. The cooking pot and the two ingredient cards stay on the stage; the working shows the factor and each ingredient in turn.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; a cooking pot with two ingredient cards, 2 cups of rice and 1 cup of dal, and a tag for 5 people; then a row of 15 guests appears beside it

marks.book: the small title card From your book appears
marks.dish: the pot with a tag for 5 people appears
marks.cards: the cards 2 cups of rice and 1 cup of dal appear
marks.guests: a row of 15 guests appears beside the pot
marks.ask: question marks appear on both cards

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is an activity from your book about cooking a dish.
<bookmark mark='dish'/>Take a dish that your family cooks for five people.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>Say it needs two cups of rice and one cup of dal.
<bookmark mark='guests'/>Fifteen guests are coming for a festival.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much of each ingredient do we need for the guests?

beats.on_screen: the pot and the guests hold still and the question marks glow

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

beats.on_screen: rice and dal drawn as two bars in the ratio 2 : 1; if only one bar grows, the pot turns a different colour

marks.ratio: the two bars rice and dal appear in the ratio 2 : 1
marks.taste: only the rice bar grows and the pot changes colour
marks.all: both bars grow together and the colour stays

narration: <bookmark mark='ratio'/>In the family dish, rice and dal are in the ratio two to one.
<bookmark mark='taste'/>If only one ingredient changes, the ratio changes and the dish tastes different.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Every ingredient must stay in proportion with the number of people.

beats.on_screen: Given: 5 people use 2 cups of rice and 1 cup of dal; 15 guests come

marks.given: the family amounts and the number of guests are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a family of five uses two cups of rice and one cup of dal. Fifteen guests are coming.

beats.on_screen: To find: the rice and the dal for 15 guests, and the rule for any dish

marks.find: the two amounts and the rule are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the rice and the dal for fifteen guests. We also want a rule that works for any dish.

beats.on_screen: factor of change = new number of people ÷ old number = 15 ÷ 5 = 3

marks.factor: the words factor of change are written

narration: <bookmark mark='factor'/>Step one, find the factor of change by dividing the new number of people by the old number.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Fifteen divided by five is three.

marks.rice: 2 × 3 = 6 cups is written under the rice card

narration: <bookmark mark='rice'/>Step two, multiply the rice by the factor. Two times three is six cups.

marks.dal: 1 × 3 = 3 cups is written under the dal card

narration: <bookmark mark='dal'/>Step three, multiply the dal by the same factor. One times three is three cups.

beats.on_screen: check: rice to dal was 2 : 1, and is now 6 : 3 = 2 : 1

marks.check: 2 : 1 and 6 : 3 = 2 : 1 are written side by side and ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the ratio of rice to dal. Six to three reduces to two to one, as before.

beats.on_screen: Answer: multiply every ingredient by the same factor, guests ÷ family size; here 6 cups of rice and 3 cups of dal

marks.here: 6 cups of rice and 3 cups of dal are written under the rule

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Multiply every ingredient by the same factor, guests divided by family size.
<bookmark mark='here'/>For this dish, fifteen guests need six cups of rice and three cups of dal.
